title: Resolving a merge conflict
summary: Exercise 4: when two branches changed the same line.

steps.title: Why conflicts happen
steps.say: Both `develop` and `issue-9-max-speed` changed `MAX_SPEED`, to different values. Git can't guess which you want, so it stops and asks you.

steps.title: Open a terminal
steps.say: These exercises are easiest in the terminal.

steps.title: Start the merge
steps.say: `cd 04-merge-conflict`, `git checkout develop`, then `git merge issue-9-max-speed`. Git says **CONFLICT**.

waitFor.hint: start the merge and see the conflict.

steps.title: Conflict markers
steps.say: Git writes **both** versions into the file, fenced off with markers.

board.code:
<<<<<<< HEAD
    public static final double MAX_SPEED = 4.5;
=======
    public static final double MAX_SPEED = 5.2;
>>>>>>> issue-9-max-speed

say.never: Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `Constants`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: Press **Ctrl+P**, type `Constants` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

steps.title: The editor helps
steps.say: Right above the conflict the editor offers **Accept Current Change**, **Accept Incoming Change** and **Accept Both Changes**. Pick one value for MAX_SPEED.

steps.title: Finish the merge
steps.say: Save, then `git add Constants.java` and `git commit`. A commit with no `-m` opens a pre-filled merge message: just save and close it.

waitFor.hint: stage and commit the resolved file.
